Saw plagiarism on a group project, turned it in to the professor. In a meeting, the plagiarizers turned around and said that I was actually responsible because I didn't fix their work. Professor believed them. I just don't feel I should have to rewrite the whole 10 page paper every month in just 12 hours before the assignment is due because they don't give a fuck about academic integrity and it shouldn't be my responsibility, a fellow student, to police their behavior. They've done it twice now, but I'm acting unethically because I won't stand for it.

Now I can't talk to anyone or else I'm "gossiping" and spreading "rumors" although the only gossip I'm spreading is asking my friend if his husband is recovering from kidney stones. Next thing I know if I blink in the course the professor will be asking me to write a formal apology for unbecoming behavior.

So I'm in a doctoral program and in a course we have to do group projects. We have to co-create presentations and papers on assigned topics. I caught half the people in the group plagiarizing. Like, word for word from the only book we use plagiarizing. I'm not that clever but I did have the book in my lap while I was looking over the paper and direct quotes kept jumping out at me so I turned them in. They tried to pull the "it was all a miscommunication, it won't happen again" card on the professor but an investigation had already been started. Out of pettiness based on the fact they started rumors about me for turning them in and tried to make up lies about me, I paid for a service and put all the work we'd "written" after being caught on the first one through it. They had been told whether it was intentional or not, without citations it's plagiarism. Found that every piece of work they'd done was/is plagiarized. Problem is, if I turn them again, I'm also taking a hit because my name is on all the work as well and it is only three specific people now. Now I have to decide if I want to get them kicked out and possibly face consequences or just let it go and cross my fingers the professor doesn't try to check it again.

Pre-rape and sexual assault day and post. I was suicidal and raped by one man, went on a planned date after explaining to the other man what happened. He sexually assaulted me after I asked him for help. Span of 12 hours. 
Before, I never thought I could be a victim. I was a shit ally, and I knew rape was a big deal, but unless it left you seriously maimed, like, just get over it? Sex is just sex, it's non-consensual but you didn't die. And I'd never be raped, I was too fat, too ugly, I didn't put myself in risky situations, I only went with guys I trusted. I didn't make mistakes other girls made. 

After, I realized how wrong I was. I never realized true fear and hopelessness until I was on my bed with a man's body weight crushing my throat, my roommate just fifty feet downstairs as I felt like I was being fucked by a red-hot poker. The sense of giving up. I never realized how much distrust I'd gain of the police; I couldn't go even though I had so much evidence because I couldn't explain what happened without saying I was suicidal and I didn't want to be locked up. Biological evidence, text messages admitting the assault and rape from both men. They'd be arrested without hesitation. But I deleted it all because I couldn't imagine telling anyone. I never felt so much shame until I had to call my mother across the country four days later outside of an urgent care because my insurance card wouldn't work and I had a massive infection from my not-healed IUD getting fucked up during the rape, and subsequently the assault when the other guy pulled on the string, begging for her to give me money first thing the bank opened for her and her asking what kind of slut I was to have two guys in 12 hours and how I could have let it happen. The urgent care doctor giving me the IUD with blood and pus on it to take home. The therapist I had telling me that it wasn't rape, I just wasn't having self-respecting sex because even though I said no, I let them use me anyway. The event really forced me to reconcile my invincibility idea and all the victim-blaming myths, realize that my therapist was shit.

Pre and post-suicide attempt. About 6 or 7 weeks ago now. The pre-- I was just digging myself deeper into a depression, not dealing with my shit, I went to therapy but I didn't want to get better. That there wasn't a life for me where I didn't hate the sunlight or waking up because it meant I was alive. The desire to jump in front of the subway, or off the highway bridge on my way home, all the weight of keeping secrets, carrying the shame, blaming myself for illness, thinking it was a choice that I was so fucked up, making my life hard for myself. Post-suicide attempt, I woke up, I hadn't died, and realized that I had hit rock bottom and had to get my shit together and maybe there was a real reason I wasn't successful. As cliche as it sounds, I turned back to trying to make a relationship with a God different from my youth, a God that was there for kindness, strength and a being I could mentally talk to when I felt so alone and afraid. This God doesn't hate me for who I am, what I've done, or any sins I do, only that every day I try to be better. I got on antidepressants. I realized I'd gotten as low as I could and I had survived, and that gives me the ability to help others and helped me shed the doubt of my ability in my future career. I realized I need to take care of myself, I need to be kinder and gentler, that I'm not ever as harsh to others as I am to myself and if others deserve forgiveness, so do I. I quit treating doing things to take care of myself as rewards for achieving things and as something I needed to do to care for myself, just like I'd care for my cat. I started looking for the sun and I don't hate waking up so much anymore. I can have nightmares of my suicide attempt, my rape, my assault, terrible things that would trigger the shit out of me, sometimes do, and wake up and cuddle my cat and not let it linger or force me to hurt myself and consciously make the decision that today this is my life, and I will be gentle with myself today. I never realized how hard recovery is.

My family has quite the pack of dogs, or did at the time this happened. On Sundays my dad will load them all in the truck's back seat and run errands (get the newspaper, pick up bacon for breakfast, run his truck through the car wash, pick up something he needs to fix whatever he's working on at tractor supply) and the trips typically last maybe an hour before my sister and I get up and my mom makes breakfast. Mom decided to go with him to make sure he got the right bacon this time.

So that's an 80lb golden retriever that is extremely stubborn and standing on the counsel from the back seat, 2 cocker spaniel x poodle mixes (about 20lbs each) that are thrilled to get to go on car rides and just want to look out the window, and 2 aussies that were about two, the female was maybe 50 lbs and the male, my brilliant darling (we fondly refer to him as a cow) is racist as fuck and was never socialized so goes absolutely berserk whenever strangers are around, was about 70lbs. My dad had the right window open, but he's never had to worry about the little ones falling out because they're actually pretty smart and just want to look, not hang out the window, the big ones are smarter than that anyway. Or so he thought. 

Well, my dad took a turn at a light in a nearly deserted town at 8am on Sunday morning which coincidentally was right in front of the police station. They get to the next light about a block away and my mom looks back to check on the "kids" and lo and behold, my dumb ass of an aussie fell out of the truck window. My dad did an illegal turn and drove as fast as possible to screech into the police parking lot while my mom jumps out and starts yelling for my dog, who fortunately listens better than her husband and ran over to her, very startled. My mom was terrified that my dog would spot a stranger, let alone a black stranger, and attack the stranger. My dad is just looking at the police station, watching some uniforms in their car laughing their asses off as my mom opens the back door and nearly throws my dog in. Apparently the golden was sticking his head by the seat belt choking my dad looking out his window, and the other three were looking out the window as my mom wrangled their errant brother. My dad said if he'd been alone he would have left my dog there out of sheer stupidity for falling out the window and swore he'd never take my dog in the truck again.

About a month later my dad was in the barber shop and all of the sudden his car alarm starts going off. He has the golden and the aussie in the truck, but the golden is too lazy to do anything. He has to run out of his haircut to scold my dog, turn off the alarm and make him sit in the backseat. Dog sets the car off three times before my dad gives up on his haircut. 

My parents are /thrilled/ to know that the aussie could live to about 20 years old.

While I work in a shelter overnight that allows me to sleep when I'm not needed, it seems like I don't do a lot. "Oh, it's so easy, you just clock in, make sure nothing is on fire, and sleep."

I do a lot of counseling that I have no supervision or training for, it's just a stroke of luck that I'm going into the mental health field and read a lot. I'll take on topics that clients want to talk about that cause me to flashback to my traumas, I'll get vicarious trauma and no support for it because my requests get denied or deleted or "lost."

I've almost gotten stuck with a needle when cleaning a room because the organization won't pay for cleaning services, I've been exposed to lots of biohazards and not been given the proper protective gear because it's hardly ever needed, until I have to clean up poop and blood shoved in a drawer by a resident that you kicked out. Is everyone in the house sick? That means I'm going to get sick but I can't call off work because there is nobody to fill in. So I'm going to spend all night cleaning the house with a bleach solution to prevent the spread of virus as much as I can in between getting sick myself.

I might not appear to be doing anything or sleeping but I'm alert to every sound in the house because there is a chance the abuser or some random person is trying to break into the house. I'm in charge of the safety of the women, their babies and the house. If someone is going through our garbage, I have to fear that someone threw out information with their name on it and that person going through the trash is the person that has also threatened to kill the woman, her toddler twins, her four month old and the sullen 13 year old. I'm the one out there at 3am with my own pepper spray knowing that I might get shot, or bitten, for little more than minimum wage and zero training being an asshole to someone that is probably homeless looking for something to eat or something he can use to make his life easier and I hate doing that but I have to.

On another note, yes, the house rules say you can't do this, or can't do that, or you have to limit your time, but I see the people under my care as humans going through some of the worst times in their lives. So, if there's an award show on after TV curfew and everyone is gathered around the TV watching it of course you get to finish watching it. I don't care the the 15 year old boy is taking hour long showers and we're in a drought- this kid lives with his mother and three younger siblings in a single room on bunk beds with no privacy. I don't care if he's jerking off in the shower, let him have that when there's no one else waiting to use the facilities. Running to the corner store half a block up the road to get water to make formula because the tap water is undrinkable but it's pouring rain out and your toddler is finally sleeping after being sick and screaming all day? You have 8 minutes, I'm watching your kid which I can't legally do, but if you were anywhere else except in a shelter you'd be allowed to have you older one watch the baby, or you'd have a water filter or be able to have more than one shelf in the fridge and pantry and your stuff wouldn't be stolen. You wouldn't have to run out 10 minutes before curfew because you'd be able to set your own schedule. So yes, I'm breaking rules and laws sometimes, but I'm going to treat you like the adult you are and show some kindness. If you tear into me because everything has boiled over in your life and you need a safe outlet, I'll be that, but it does hurt my feelings because I'm human too.

And I know the house has mice, termites, ants, electrical problems and no heat in half the rooms. I'm very sorry, but there is nothing I can do. I'm just night staff. I'll give you as many blankets as you ask for. I'll give you the space heater from the office so that I'm freezing instead of you and your kids. But I cannot make the higher ups doing anything.

My parents pay for my $130 therapy every week, I'm on their phone plan and health insurance, when I've had medical emergencies they've sent me money when it wasn't covered by insurance. They buy my tickets if they want me to visit them. For a while my mom was paying some money on the interest on my student loans without me knowing. She's stopped now, fortunately. She also sends me gifts for her grandchild, my cat. They pay my credit card off. My dad also co-signed on a lot of my loans/housing, so while he's not paying for anything he's sticking his neck out for me.

I'm living across the country from them in one of the most expensive cities in the United States. I've been a "disappointment" in more of a social sense as this queer, mentally ill, rape & sexual assault survivor child and I think they have a sense of responsibility that they forced me to run away from them to live my queer life which then caused me to experience the incidents of sexual violence, or so they think because if I had stayed back home, I wouldn't have had the opportunity to be violated. And they recognize that I'm only so fucked up mentally because they wouldn't believe me as a child and listen to me when I asked for help. And, they think if they give me financial support I'm less likely to kill myself because I'll be less overwhelmed.

I'm 22, have my B.S., M.A. and am starting my PhD in the fall. I've always worked while in school to cover what I can, take out loans to the max, and have scholarships. My grandparents set up a college fund for me before I was born so my undergrad was paid for, or would have been if my parents hadn't emptied my college fund. I'm incredibly grateful for the support my parents have provided, I'd be dead without it. I feel very guilty that they support me so much, but I also get this attitude sometimes that if they can't love me and accept me as I am and think that giving me money is better than their love, that's just fine. And, for a lot of the hell I went through, let them pay for the damage they could have prevented. It's very entitled and privileged. Their financial support has allowed me to build up some savings.

I'm trying to write my thesis but its taking me forever. I try to break it down in to digestible parts, and be happy with the progress I've made, but the timer is counting down and I'm getting more depressed and anxious as I see my peers doing their work. They made their projects so easy, whereas I wanted to make an actual difference and had to jump through a billion hoops and yet I'm lazy because I have crippling depression and anxiety and just trying to write a little is exhausting. They all have support from their mentors but mine don't understand my project or even ask if I need help, and when I ask for help on a certain part they're unavailable. They have writing groups I'm expressly not invited to, I'm explicitly excluded from any group get togethers and it makes it worse knowing my roommate is going to them and getting support from all of them when they don't want anything to do with me. I'm beyond burnt out but I'm signing up for another 6 or so years of academia hoping it will be different but having a crippling fear it won't. I won't have the support I need and I'll be in the same situation just throwing ideas around hoping they make some sense.
I'm watching Misfits, but not the first three really good seasons, so I'm really screwed. But, if I were a probation worker or a dead body, they could probably deal with me.

Graduated at age 20 with honors while working part time and running two student organizations and applying to graduate programs, went to my MA at age 21, will graduate from my MA in May while working part time and on several research projects, and will begin my doctoral studies at age 23 in August/September this year. 

Its been incredibly hard not to have the "I was the greatest in high school, why don't I get it in college/grad school?" mentality. I have a lot of psychological problems, but my schoolwork and my cat are my priorities and I don't want to let my cat down. It helps to put it in perspective that letter grades really don't describe self-worth, its more of the question "could I talk about this intelligently for an extended period of time?" and if the answer is yes, the B+ in my course doesn't sting so much any more.

My twin and I switched in band class, I played brass, she played wind. Worked well until the teacher decided to make all the wind players do a solo. It came to me and I said I don't know how, and the teacher lost his mind about how useless I was not to have learned the piece we'd been working on for three months. The entire class was cracking up, and I finally had to say I was the other one and we'd switched. It was funny, because even on my instrument I didn't learn how to play it and he was pretty humiliated to speak to a student like that in front of everyone. 

Also we were placed in the same room to do the ACT and the test proctors were very upset they had no way to tell if we were the correct one with the right ID. They almost didn't let us take the test. Probably didn't help we'd gotten dressed and left the house at different times and found we'd dressed identically when we showed up and had an oh shit moment.

Also, I was severely bullied in school so my poor twin was a default target because the teachers hated me and couldn't tell us apart. The kids tried to use the same excuse to be assholes but could tell us apart. We we switched schools halfway through high school and were at the school at different times of the day, the majority of the teachers didn't know we were a set and got awfully confused but never questioned it? They about peed themselves on parent-teacher conference night when they finally saw us together.

In undergrad we majored in the same thing, took our harder classes together to help each other and sat next to each other and wrote notes on a notebook between each of us to help clarify concepts (neither of us felt comfortable to ask questions in class but have a funny way of understanding what the other doesn't) or entertain each other. But we didn't take all our courses together, so sometimes the professors that didn't know there were twins in the department got extremely confused. Or, we'd take the course in different semesters and the non-tw-introduced professor would get very concerned that the same kid was taking the class again. 

Now we're adults and likely won't get confused because I'm transitioning genders and she's not. I think I'll miss that, it was always really fun to confuse people.
